utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we are starting with the response by the Prosecution to the joint Defence motion for leave to assign a new military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Defence have filed a joint motion seeking leave to assign a new military expert witness pursuant to Rule 94 bis. I say at the outset -- I won't be very long but I say at the outset the Prosecution does not oppose a Defence request to call expert evidence on a relevant topic, which is before the Trial Chamber, which requires the development of expert expertise. The Defence motion seems to say that the motion -- the report or expert's report it filed earlier of Colonel Barasin's would fall within the category which it is now trying to -- in which it is now trying to call a Defence witness. The Trial Chamber last year proprio moto rejected the filing of Colonel Barasin's report, I think describing it as "unhelpful". An objective reading of that report would indicate that it wasn't doing quite what the Defence wanted it to do or indicates they are trying to do now, that is to file objective expert testimony in relation to the conflict in Bosanski Samac in 1992 and 1993, and expert evidence as to the role and function of the military or militaries during the indictment period relating to the conflicting parties. At this stage of the trial, the Prosecutor still of course at the end of it has to prove that there was an international armed conflict in relation to the Article 2 charge, which only of course relates to the charge of unlawful deportation or transfer -- sorry the unlawful transfer because deportation is of course a charge under Article 5 which doesn't require an international armed conflict. So it relates only to a very small portion of the entire Prosecution case, that is the transfer of people not over the border into Croatia but to other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time. The test -- withdraw that. The Prosecutor filed a motion in 1998 for this Trial Chamber or the pre-Trial Chamber to take judicial notice of the internationality of the conflict. The pre-Trial Chamber said it had to be proved at trial. That was in 1999 and subsequent to that of course it's been the Aleksovski judgement. I'll just hand up copies of the relevant pages of the judgement to assist the Trial Chamber and my learned friends as to the appropriate test. If I can take Your Honours to page 52. The previous page said what is the applicable law on this issue and the Appeals Chamber in paragraph 125, about halfway down, set out what is important is whether the subsequent case, the legal principle enunciated in the Tadic judgement has to "overall control" may be applied in relation to the conflict between the Bosnian Croats and the Bosnian Muslims in Bosnia-Herzegovina and so on. Down the page, the same question arises from the facts of the instant case, that is the level of control by a state --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down while reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That is the level of control by state or entity [Croatia or the army of the -- I apologise, Your Honour, the hard copy of the judgement I have of the next page is missing and I have handed up a printout. Could I borrow one of the Defence ones for one moment? Thank you, Mr. Usher. The words I was using, Croatia or the army of the Republic of Croatia, HV, or a military group, the HVO, that was engaged in an armed conflict that was prima facie internal. It is therefore perfectly proper in the instant case to record and rely upon the legal principle enunciated in the Tadic judgement. The Appeal's Chamber's conclusion was that it was Aleksovski applying the Tadic principle was that it was the overall control test which was the important one. I emphasise that is subsequent to the earlier motion in this case. And of course, Your Honours have heard a great deal of evidence, including of course in the Defence case, led from the various Defence witnesses, of a conflict occurring between the Republic of Croatia or forces under the control of the Republic of Croatia, whether it be the HVO or the HV, that is the Republic of Croatia army itself. In fact, as recently as Friday, we heard evidence from the witness sitting here at the moment as to Croatian shelling and the involvement of the troops of the Republika Srpska against troops from the Republic of Croatia. So I just say, I put that in -- put it into context. There has been a lot of evidence in this case as to a conflict and shells going backwards and forwards across the Sava River into Bosanski Samac and fighting on the ground between the forces of the two armies and of course there has also been reference to forces of the Bosnian federal -- the Bosnian state army, the ABiH. So if the Defence are to present such evidence, it has to be highly relevant and on the point, that is that there was no international armed conflict at the relevant time between the -- Croatia, Serbia, the Bosnian government, the HVO, or whatever other forces not alleged to be involved in the international armed conflict which the Defence apparently is saying did not occur during the indictment period. That's the first point. The second point is as to the scope outside of the internationality question of the expertise or the evidence given on the role of the military. Now, the Prosecution of course has no objection to -- it couldn't -- to the Defence calling proper military expert of the military expert -- evidence of the command and control within the JNA or the Republika Srpska forces, the VRS, or any other army. It may be helpful to the Trial Chamber and it is certainly something the Prosecution would not object to. However we do take issue with the statement that paragraph 4 of the Defence motion, that "authoritatively identifying a conflict" and "international armed conflict" requires a great deal of scholarship, expertise, and investigation. The Prosecution submission will be in this particular case, the facts very much speak for themselves. But if they are to produce another report, in our submission it has to be confined to the relevant issues and it cannot stray into the areas which Colonel Barasin's attempted report did, that is making many assertions, conclusions, and statements which were not supported by evidence or which did not show the facts or the underlying facts upon which the conclusions were based, which is in great contrast to the expert reports the Prosecution put in, those of Dr. Tabeau and Dr. Donia which were academically rigorous studies, properly footnoted and properly sourced, so the summary the Prosecution doesn't object to a proper expert's report if it is so confined to the relevant issue, that is whether or not it was international and command and control issues within the JNA and the VRS. Those are my submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. The Trial Chamber will give its ruling in due course. In the meantime, we proceed with the witness, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, yes. Further cross-examination by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Savic.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We won't go for very long today. I hope you've had a rest over the weekend. I just have a few more questions and then I'll finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P127, please, ter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While the document is being looked for, this is an information that you've signed, Prosecutor asked you on Friday, on page 45, whether in relation to this information you're stating that the Crisis Staff was the one who organised the documents regarding the persecutions and you said yes it was. Now, can you have a look at this information? If you can find the place, whether it says anywhere that the Crisis Staff, that is the War Presidency, was the one that was implementing the documents of persecution against the non-Serb population? Can you please find the place where it actually says that.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On which page?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. You have to find it. I'm saying that there isn't such an information. You said to the Prosecutor that when you were writing this information, you said that this was the -- done by the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency, now what I'm saying is that I want you to find out this in this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, we have difficulty seeing one another around this column that we have between us. Just as a matter of clarification, it might well just be the translation, but I'm a little confused as to page 6, lines -- well, 3 and 4, concerning the Crisis Staff -- this is your question, Mr. Pantelic, where you are talking about the Crisis Staff, then you say that is the War Presidency, and you go on to talk about it implementing the documents of persecution. I'm sorry, I'm not with you. I say it might be a matter of translation but what are the documents of persecution against the non-Serb population? If you could maybe clarify for me, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. I didn't say that in that form so maybe it's a matter for translation. I will clarify it. I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Savic, you said to the Prosecutor on Friday, on page 45, when you were discussing this document, you said that the Crisis Staff, and later on the War Presidency, practically implemented a campaign of discrimination and terror against the non-Serb population. Now, what I'm asking you here in this information that among other things you signed, is there anywhere, can you find it anywhere, exactly the part where it says -- which is relating to the Crisis Staff, that is the War Presidency, that they were the one who is were implementing this? So I'm not talking about the volunteers, I'm not talking the police, you were explaining this. What I'm interested in directly is precisely this part. Please.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 2, paragraph 2, it says, "From the beginning of the war, to start with the Crisis Staff and later on the War Presidency of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, came under the influence of a couple of individuals."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, this is just an information -- this is just an information which had a purpose, to point to certain things, as I've explained, to some negative occurrences to some things that the army wasn't in agreement with. But who was responsible for the deportation, for people being relocated? I think it's the Crisis Staff that's responsible for that. That's my opinion but I don't know that. Perhaps it's somebody else. [Realtime transcript read in error "Q."] Who else would be the most responsible for that part of the work other than the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is just your assumption, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, it would probably occur as a problem here in the transcript because last sentence that the witness said was who else would be the most responsible for that part, and here it is recorded as a question so this might suggest that it was a question posed by Mr. Pantelic, so it should be corrected instead of Q in front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's a continuation of the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this wasn't heard when I asked you. This is -- this was just your assumption?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's my opinion, my assumption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm finished with this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Further on, Mr. Re asked you regarding the telegrams, that is a series of telegrams of the 17th Corps of the 2nd Military District and so on, in those telegrams, you explained to him, and to me, that the term of the Serb TO doesn't exist. This was just an assumption of the commander Nikolic and Simo Zaric and so on and those parts in those telegrams. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I said I remember that in Samac, there was no Serb TO, no Serb TO in Samac. But I do recall that in Batkusa they were established and they called themselves staff of the Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I haven't asked the question yet. Just slow down.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: P21, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It would be convenient for the interpreters' booth maybe we could have English version on the ELMO so that they can follow and the B/C/S version in front of the witness. So it's up to our friends from --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, the interpreters would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it would be familiar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe because the interpreters would like to have --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could Mr. Pantelic point me to the page in the transcript where I referred to this document? I'm just having some difficulty locating it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is -- Your Honour, the topic is the Serbian TO in the events between -- in the night 16 to 17. I have in fact three documents to discuss with this witness with regard to that issue because there are some chronologically issues which should be clarified, the previous statement of this witness. It's P21, P22, P23, and P19. In fact, these are the four documents, military documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re is asking where in the page of the transcript he referred to those matters in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Specifically this document, P23, I don't recall asking the witness about this particular document. I'm just asking my learned friend can point me to the page in the transcript where I did. I just can't find it at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, if I may clarify, sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, in fact, I'm referring to the topic in general terms. In order to clarify certain details in this topic, I have to make reference to these four documents. So that is the basis of the introduction or discussion of these documents with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Re? You're still --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I do object to that. I asked the witness about two specific documents, there are obviously other documents in evidence. It is unclear what Mr. Pantelic's purpose is. I showed the witness two documents, that doesn't entitle him then to go on and ask the witness about other unrelated documents written by other people perhaps referring to the same events. In my submission, there is no forensic purpose that can arise in relation to these other documents because I didn't refer to them in relation to affecting the interests of his client in re-cross-examination as opposed to the chance he had in cross-examination. There is simply nothing in the other documents which arose, in my submission, affecting the interests of his client because I didn't refer to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you are talking about documents P21?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: P23, the one which Mr. Pantelic is now referring to, and the other one. I referred to two of the four. I took the witness through two of the four. The other two I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you are objecting in relation to P23.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And P21?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure about P21.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean, I don't know, maybe my learned friend --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Let me hear from Mr. Re first.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which particular documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I took the witness to P19 and the document that Major General Jankovic signed, which is -- excuse me. P23. So P23 and P19. P19 and P23 were the two document I took the witness to, the one by Jankovic and the one -- and the other one. I can't see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my learned friend --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Those are the two documents, P19 ter and P23 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My learned friend on Friday, it's at page 51, line -- it's line 12 until 16, he asked this witness with regard to the Croatian forces coming from Republic of Croatia, attempting an infantry attack across the bridge. This witness said no, there was no such forces. And furthermore, all the topics raised by the Prosecution with this witness, with regard to the involvement of the elements of 17th Tactical Group and with regard to the operation in the night between 16 and 17 April, was discussed quite detailed with this witness. So we cannot see isolated, for example, one document which is P19, which is a telegram between -- telegram sent by command of 17th corps to the higher command, without knowing the special report of the superior command sent only half -- one hour and a half before this document. So in terms of clarification, we have in totality, I have -- analysis of various documents, exhibits, in order to find the right solution and to finally challenge, if I may say, even the credibility of this witness, because with this stage, with these proceedings we can only find the two. Not to mention in the previous proceedings, during re-examination, for example, our learned friend, Ms. Reidy introduced on numerous occasions various documents through the witnesses during re-examination. So it won't be take long. I will just make a point in these four documents which may assist this Trial Chamber in relation to the -- these proceedings and specifically with regard to my client, because I will emphasise again, the position of the Defence of Mr. Blagoje Simic is that he is -- he was not a part of this military operation, by any means, and I have to defend my client, I have to properly present his Defence, and that's why, because this is a practically last military witness, fact witness, from Samac. He was a former commander for the detachment -- from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Pantelic, the Trial Chamber will allow you to explore that possibility of the Defence for your client in relation to -- I'm sure it's in relation to the role of the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Savic, you see before you an interim report of the 17th of April of the command of the 2nd Military District, seated in Sarajevo. This interim report was delivered to the operation centre of the Main Staff of the armed forces of the SFRY. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this for the very first time. It's like -- yes, it is as you say. It's probably that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, whatever I ask you in relation to these documents I am not asking you only whether you've seen these documents before but whether this is what it says in the document and the Trial Chamber will assess because this is the Prosecution document, they will see whether this is authoritative.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excellent. In this document, do you see anywhere mentioned Crisis Staff of the Bosanski Samac municipality and Pelagicevo, that they have taken over the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of the day, it says there are indications that the enemy could strike against, steps are being taken to prevent the attack and disarm the remaining enemy forces. That's what it says. And civilian authorities being established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of this report, it says that the vital facilities have been taken in the night of the 17th of April. Is this -- is this correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further on, it says that because of many conflicts and incidents that preceded the attempt of the Croatian forces to cross over the Sava River, that that would be basis for the intervention. That's the second sentence. Do you agree with the second sentence?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just find the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to this line of questioning. As I understand it, Your Honour's ruling was confined to the Crisis Staff and things which affected the interests of Mr. Pantelic's client. This is going through line by line and asking whether the witness agrees with someone else's document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because, Your Honour, in response to a question of my learned friend, this witness said there was not any action of the Croatian forces across the bridge. That was his answer to the question of my learned friend. And now we have another evidence with completely different angle. So I just want to clarify it with the witness, is it true or not, what was said in this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps to expedite matters, the witness can read on his own and then you ask -- you put the question to him because the documents are before the Trial Chamber. They are part of the evidence so we can read instead of reading line by line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But otherwise, you are within your rights to proceed with the questioning of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Savic, as we read this document, which was created on the basis of some reports from the field, tell me, on the basis of your personal knowledge, were any attempts made by the Croatian armed forces to cross the bridge on the Sava River?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian Army, from Croatia, I don't think that they made any attempts to cross the bridge on the Sava. I don't know about that. But the Croatian artillery did target the town of Samac. That's what I said. But it was on the Bosna River on the bridge near Prud where they tried to carry out an attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is the next proposition, it has to do with Prud, so we've clarified that. Now, on the basis of your very own knowledge, the elements of the 17th Tactical Group and then of the Serb TO and the militia, did they take the vital facilities in the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the elements of the tactical group. If you're referring to the 4th Detachment, I am sure, and I claim, that none of us took any facilities. Later on, we tried to keep them by engaging men from the detachment and that was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Furthermore, what is your personal knowledge in this regard, that isolated persons opened fire at the Serb forces and at citizens? Because that is what this report also says. Were there any such situations after the 17th?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand your question. What does this mean, "isolated persons"? What are you trying to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what it says in this military document. You're an officer. I don't know either. You explain this to us. What is your understanding of this?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my highest level was up to the TG and Ninkovic [as interpreted] and contacts with him. But all the rest, higher levels, I have no idea who wrote what and all that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, I think we have a bit of a confusion here in terms of the use of this word "isolated." Because the English translation of the document that I have in front of me talks about "individuals who opened fire on our forces and citizens have been isolated." But in your question to Mr. Savic, in the translation, you're talking about isolated persons doing the firing, which is not in keeping with the document. I can't see the line off-hand now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean page 15, line 14 and 15?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Exactly right, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's a matter of translation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. Because in your question as translated it talks -- you're asking about isolated persons opening fire, which doesn't make any sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Maybe that's a matter of translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And just one small correction in the transcript on page 15, line 23, here it says "and Ninkovic" and it's referring to Colonel Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Instead of Ninkovic the name should be Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Mr. Savic, it says here persons who are isolated and who opened fire against our citizens in town. Just tell me, did this happen in Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say -- also it says here that there were cases that civilians moved out, did that happen?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further on it says here in the telegram that many members of the former municipal leadership fled to the Republic of Croatia. Do you have any personal knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Savic, you see the stamp down here on this document, the date is the 17th of April, 1992. It says that it was sent at 1545 hours, is that not being contested?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have now document P19, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: While that's being brought up, just going back to this term "isolated," your question again on lines 20 and 21, again might be a translation problem. But the way it reads, again, is not in keeping with the document because your question to Mr. Savic is: "It says here persons who are isolated and who opened fire against our citizens in town." The document, on the other hand, which now has disappeared off the screen in front of me talked about persons who opened fire against our forces and citizens, and just doing this by memory now, and who have been isolated. So they opened fire and then they were isolated. The way again it reads now is these persons were isolated and then they opened fire. Which is in contradistinction to what the actual document is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. So I will put this question on English. Maybe that will be clarify the situation, or I clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: No. I don't think you need to do that, Mr. Pantelic, but just for the sake of the record I was just saying that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: But we have the document. I don't think it serves any purpose in --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Maybe we could have the English version on the ELMO for the benefit of the interpreters and then the B/C/S version in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in this document that was sent, you see the stamp, it was at 1730 on the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question? I didn't hear what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at the stamp down here. You can see that this stamp was sent or received, received practically, on the 17th of April, at 1730 hours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the previous document, right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document of the 17th Corps, informing the commander of the 2nd Military District in Sarajevo, where Kukanjac is commander and they inform him about the situation in the area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that document, it also says that members of the TO and the MUP of the Serb municipality took control of certain facilities. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, in this document, it says that forces from the Republic of Croatia attempted an infantry attack across the bridge. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here but it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now, please, document P23, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, until the document is found, here was the 4th Detachment collect information from the area of responsibility of your --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down. This is too fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat the question. You from the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment, you collect information and you send it to the superior command or rather the 17th Tactical Group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The command of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, remember to pause and the witness should also pause after listening to your question before beginning to answer. The interpreters are having difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Savic, could you please pause a few seconds after my question and then answer. The same goes for me. So my question was the following: When the commander of the 17th Tactical Group collects information from the ground, from all detachments, then it compiles some kind of daily report of its own and then it sends it further on to the corps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the 17th Corps from its own tactical groups, the operative group 1 from the 17th Tactical Group, et cetera, collects all information, then they send a daily report to the 2nd military district in Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is the following: All information that comes to the 17th Tactical Group, inter alia, includes information from the 4th Detachment from the ground. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why would anybody then, along these higher lines, forge or change information because you have just said that you do not -- that you do not --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please wait for the end of the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: First of all, these datas have been faked, and if they are fake who faked them and why fake them? This is nothing that this witness could be aware about. He already said that his highest command was 17th Tactical Group and anything further in this military here is something unknown to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic, you did ask in fact the witness earlier on that the 17th Tactical Group command collected information from other detachments as well, so -- and the witness did explain his level of knowledge. He was only dealing with the 4th Detachment. So that was only one segment. So these reports from the higher command which was above him cannot be explained by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If your 17th Tactical Group informs the corps about the following that in the zone of responsibility of the 4th Detachment certain things are going on, who can this -- who can the 17th Tactical Group get this information from if it's not the 4th Detachment? In which way, just tell me that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, how they do this, how they sent their reports, now the 17th TG towards their superior command, how they reported, I have no idea. They can write whatever they want. I really have no idea, but what went from the field was correct information. I was in Samac and I know that we reported about what was going on and so on and so forth. And now what kind of report was received ultimately is something I have no idea about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, from the 4th Detachment, who sent reports from the field to the 17th Tactical Group? Who was in charge of that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander, his deputy, the assistant commander, the duty officer, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at the document that's in front of you, on page 1, this is the command of the 17th Corps, the 18th of April. In paragraph 3, the Prosecutor asked you the same thing, that between the 17th and 18th of April, that the Serb units of the TO and the police were carrying out actions against the paramilitaries in Samac. Is that correct? Is that correct on the basis of what you know from the field?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operations against?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 18th of April, by 11.00, the above-mentioned forces took Samac in its entirety? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Underneath that there is a paragraph where it says that the command of TG 17 was ordered to secure the success attained and not to take any other offensive measures. That is in keeping with what you said, that you were given this task not to do anything.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as the higher command is concerned, this operation was a success, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained this. I don't know what higher levels wrote to their own even higher levels. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 2? There is a conclusion, that is item 8, and then another sentence, "The corps units responded to paramilitary group's activities, operational group 1" -- we are not interested in that -- "and engaged in routing the paramilitary groups in Bosanski Samac and establishing the civilian authorities [Tactical Group 17]." Is that what actually happened in Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, when you are reading or explaining or even asking the question, please do it slowly. Otherwise, the record won't be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my question was that the 17th Tactical Group was engaged in routing paramilitary formations in Bosanski Samac and establishing the civilian authority. And your answer on page 23, line 2, it says -- your answer was that you don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit P24?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document, in this telegram, the command of the 17th Corps again reports to the 2nd Military District on the 18th of April, sometime at about 1740 hours -- in fact 1725 hours, and under item 4, it says that "Serb forces of the Bosanski Samac TO together with the MUP forces by 1100 hours they took control over the entire town." Is this in accordance with your personal knowledge about what happened in Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further on, below that, it says that "The tactical group commander was ordered to secure the success that has been achieved and to abstain from taking any special steps." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't know what was ordered to the commander of the T -- of TG 17, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber how come you're saying now that you agree with the statement that the forces of the Serb TO took part in that, while throughout this time, both to the Prosecutor and to me, you've been denying the existence of the Serb TO forces, although Mr. Zaric says that -- said that in his interview? Now, what do you mean when you said that you agreed that the Serb TO forces took part in this?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll repeat. The Serb TO forces in Samac, in the 4th Detachment, did not exist. They did not exist. The 4th Detachment did not take part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment. I have to interrupt. You've been saying that TO forces did not exist. We have been listening to you for two days and now you agree with me that TO forces of Bosanski Samac, Serb TO forces and MUP forces, by 1100 hours, they have taken over the entire town. You just confirmed that two minutes ago. Again I'm asking you: What is the truth, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that this question of Mr. Pantelic, although I don't have a problem with it, it's a bit premature. First of all we have to establish what is the understanding of this witness of the term "Serbian TO" and then ask him this question, otherwise we really don't know what we are talking about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps the witness can explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please explain, what are, for you, Serbian forces? Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb TO forces, according to what I know, they are members of a unit that was established, I believe, in Batkusa and they were led by Mico Ivanovic, also known as Mijak. And according to my assessment, I believe that these are these force that had come together with these men, shall I call them volunteers, MUP people, they came to Samac on that day. And so they established what does it say here, and they have taken over the entire town, that's what it says in this report. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, is this your knowledge or is this your opinion? Is this your assumption? Because precisely this is what you mentioned in your answer.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of days later --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Just very briefly, is this your personal knowledge or is this your assumption Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the first detachment as part of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of that detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it was Mico Ivanovic, also known as Mijak, and after that was Savo Bosic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 1st Detachment was part of the 17th Tactical Group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prosecutor asked you on page 51 on Friday whether on 17th of April there were forces came from Croatia across the bridge, Croatian forces, and you answered that there were no such forces. Tell me, what did you do on the 17th of April, around 3.00 in the morning, you personally?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had just got up at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness has already explained that so many times, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The point is, Your Honour, I finished with this issue absolutely, the point is that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll just ask you this question: If you were sleeping at 3.00 in the morning, how come that you don't -- you know there were no Croatian forces that were about to attack Samac, as it says in all the telegrams of the 17th Tactical Group and the 17th corps and all the other telegrams? If you were asleep, how do you know that there were no Croatian forces about to attack? Can you explain this to the Trial Chamber? Because the whole detachment was asleep. Can you explain how do you know?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained that. I came to the command in about a quarter of an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment. Before 3.00 a.m. while were you asleep, how do you know, on the basis of what do you claim, that it was not possible that there was an attack that was going to be launched across the bridge on the Sava River from Croatia? Could you please explain.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you're asleep, it's 3.00 a.m. 17th of April, 1992. I'm asking you, while you were asleep, how do you know that Croatian forces are not amassing on the other side, across the Sava River, and are about to attack? Because -- that's what I'm asking you because it's all of these telegrams of serious generals, that's what it says. So I'm asking you: How do you know there were no Croatian forces that were about to attack Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had an information about the movement of forces from the Republic of Croatia, about their amassment, in a certain direction. We had this information and we received some information from the tactical group and also some intelligence from our local citizens. And as I said, that the attack on the 17th was not an infantry attack from Croatia or any other except the artillery shelling of the town of Samac, and that is what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you cannot state with certainty what happened before 3.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. What I heard at the command -- that's what I heard at the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, you were asleep, you couldn't have known. You were asked by the Prosecutor on page 43, about the fact that the JNA was practically inactive and that that's how it allowed a new regime to be established based on discriminatory basis. Your answer was we knew about that. Now what I'm asking you, the Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo in establishing, according to your knowledge, according to your information, your personal attitude, is this also a discriminatory -- ethnically-discriminatory establishment, institution?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a part of that Serb municipality and you are still today?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. That's where I am, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a municipality a part of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why in your opinion the Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo is that an ethnically-discriminatory establishment?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object. Is my learned friend Mr. Pantelic referring to -- I think the witness's answer was referring to April 1992. This latest question appears to be directed to the situation today, which is irrelevant for the purposes of cross-examination and the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. My question was directed to the period 1992, the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo, strictly on that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking you a question. Large number of delegates founded the Serb municipality. Why is it, in your opinion, that it is a discriminatory institution?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because many people of other ethnicities left Bosanski Samac, as some people say they have been expelled, and you've mentioned another term, isolated, detained, that's the reason why I think this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This institution, this municipality, did they do that or was it some other factors?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think a different organs of municipality, not the municipality but organs of authority. First of all, I mean MUP or SUP, the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that is a matter for debate. Now, Mr. Savic, can you tell me something else. Why did you deny throughout this time -- what was your motive for denying all the fact from these tell grams of the 17th Tactical Group and the higher commands?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Why have you denied? This kind of question, I don't really think is appropriate. The witness is testifying here. He's not denying or approving or doing whatever. He's giving his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because, Your Honour, after this question, I would like to put on the record that all the testimony of this witness should be stricken because he's absolutely unreliable witness and that was the position of the Defence, due to the fact and the answers and contradictions that he made so --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. Savic, I'm asking you --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution objects very strongly to this gratuitous attack upon a witness who is giving evidence and is being asked to comment upon other people's documents, that's as high as it can possibly get. The witness can agree or disagree. I would ask Mr. Pantelic to withdraw his last comment. It's unbecoming for counsel in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Actually, there is no basis for the comments of Mr. Pantelic against this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, that would be a matter for the final evaluation of the testimony of this witness during the procedure of rendering of judgement. So my last question to this witness is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please tell me, Mr. Savic, why did you lie to this Trial Chamber in relation to the fact that the elements of the 17th Tactical Group took part in the attack on Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object. I object to this question very strongly. First of all, the way the question is posed, why did you lie, suggests that the witness was actually lying. First of all, I don't believe that this is what the witness was doing here, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, if a witness gives you an answer which contradicts your instructions, it does not necessarily mean that the witness is telling lies and that's not the proper way of putting it to the witness. And you are finished, so please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I finished. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic? Or is it Mr. Pisarevic for re-examination? Re-examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Savic.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the Trial Chamber to draw the attention of Mr. Pantelic, Defence counsel of Mr. Blagoje Simic, about the way that he is talking to the witnesses, especially we witnessed here Mr. Pantelic asking questions in an unprofessional way, being very rude to the witnesses of Mr. Simo Zaric, that is that the witnesses for the Defence of Mr. Simo Zaric is bringing here to testify. This was seen a moment ago, although a couple of times his attention was drawn to this. However, I am grateful to the Trial Chamber for protecting the witnesses from such attacks. Mr. Savic, are you aware of the fact that at the assembly of the Serb municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo in establishing, there was an -- even just one deputy of other ethnicity except for Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question that I'm going to ask you: Are you aware of the fact that for the Staff Commander of the TO of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation, Mico Ivanovic, also known as Mijak, was appointed?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mico told me about this later. He told me this himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were speaking about the existence of the HDZ units and SDA units, armed units, you mentioned at one point that there were also some units that were armed of the SDS, there were some armed men who were members of the SDS. You started telling us something about some men and you said you had some personal knowledge. Can you please just clarify this very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I started to talk about this, one of you interrupted me, and what I know is that in the villages, there was a group of young men who had undergone some training. And I know from my village, four or five of them, they were members of the SDS party, and they were members of the staff that we spoke about earlier, this unit that was led by Mico Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the names of these men that you know for sure were members of this unit?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know these young men because they were from my village. There were a lot younger than I am. I know them all. Zeljko Djuric; Petar Lukic; Cedo Lukic; Caslav, Ilic; Milos Savic, also known as Mrki, he's a relative of mine. So there were four or five of them -- in fact five, five that I know of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is just from your village?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's just from my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the information that there were young men from other villages?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information is that there were young men from every village, depending on the number of inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Here you were shown telegrams sent by military units and as I have noticed, these were mostly telegrams of the 17th Corps of the JNA, and telegrams of the 2nd Military District that were sent to the Main Staff. Did anyone show you here that some report went from the 17th Tactical Group, addressed to the 17th Corps of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reports that I had a look at here, I will repeat, this is the first time that I see them here, this is the first time I've heard of them. In parts of these reports I only disagreed with some details, because I did not have any influence as to how the command of the 17th Tactical Group would write this report in what content and how it will go to a higher command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, can you just identify which reports you're dealing with here for the record to make sense. Is it the same ones discussed, P19, P21, P23?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P19, P21, and P23.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two words are used here, telegrams and reports. What is this, this that you have been shown, namely Exhibits P19, P21, and P23? Are these telegrams or are these reports?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I could see, it seemed obvious that these reports were written by some kind of duty officers, not by the unit commander?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown these exhibits, P19 ter, P21 and P23 ter?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This isn't an objection but there was also P24 in there as well, there were actually four documents which Mr. Pantelic referred to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please take a look at P19. What does it say here? Who sent this, who wrote this telegram or this report the way you've been putting it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is written by the commander of the 17th Corps, and it is signed by the leader of the duty team, Colonel Pedisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who writes this telegram, this Mr. Pedisic or the commander of the 17th Corps?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is compiled by the duty officer who signed it, but in the upper left-hand corner, it says in whose name in which this is written but it is signed by the signatory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is the commander of the 17th Corps that's sending this. Now I'm asking you the following: What it says here in this text, is this compiled by the gentleman who signed it and does he do it on his own without any consultations, without any approval from his commander, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you. I had no insight in how they worked, how could I? But the person who signed the text compiled it. That's the way it should have been, that is the person who was supposed to stand behind this text, the gentleman who signed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Pisarevic, these are matters outside the knowledge of this witness because he was not one of the persons compiling these reports or telegrams, as you want to refer to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell me when was this telegram sent, at what time?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1700 hours -- is it 1730? I can't read it very well. It's not very legible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was sent to the 2nd army district of the JNA as we've already put it. Thank you. Could we just have a look at it now? Could we look at document P23 ter now? Who is it addressed to, who was sending this, and to whom?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Command of the 17th Corps is sending this to the command of the 2nd Military District, to the operations officer on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can see this properly, 1945.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who signed this?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I supposed to answer this? I mean, I couldn't hear things very well. So it is commander General Savo Jankovic, Major General Savo Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a report, isn't it? When it is signed by the commander of the unit.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we agree that when telegrams are sent, they are signed by duty officers, operations officers, in units? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the commander is not there, then it is done by the duty officer, but then if the commander is there, then he approves or he says well, you sign it and send it on. That's the way it was where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's take a look at this third document, P23. I'm sorry, P21, sorry. This is the commander of the 2nd Military District to the general staff of the army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who signed this?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The senior commanding officer, the duty team, Colonel Nikola Sego.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that the commander of the 2nd military district of the Yugoslav People's Army was General Kukanjac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just tell me at what time this report was sent.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1545. It's not really legible. Maybe it's 1845, it's a poor copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th, right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice that the report of the 2nd Military District was sent before the 17th Corps sent the 2nd Military District its report on how they viewed what happened on the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 17th Corps, 17, 26, 2nd District, 1545. I can't see the date here. It seems to me that this report went first, I mean the one that we just discussed -- I mean it can be seen according to the dates involved, and then on the 18th, this report went from the command of the 17th Corps so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So reports did not go along the following lines that first they had to come from the lowest ranking units and then to the higher ranking units. It would happen that through other sources, they would obtain some information and then send their reports. The only source was not the report of the lower ranking units, the detachments, et cetera, in order to have the higher ranking units compile their own reports, can we agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to attorney Pantelic's question, you said on page 71, dated the 20th of March, he asked you about a RUP 2 or RUP 12, and you said that you were not an expert for this kind of technical equipment and signals equipment, but I am going to ask you the following -- I'm going to ask you two things actually. One is the following: Through this equipment that was in the command of the 4th Detachment, did you maintain communication throughout, for about a month, and after what happened in Bosanski Samac, I mean you were commander for a longer period of time. So is it through this equipment that you communicated with the command of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This particular piece of equipment. Now what its name is is something I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this reorganisation took place and when the Army of Republika Srpska was established, for a while you were commander of the 5th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your superior command was the 2nd Posavina Brigade, whose command was in Pelagicevo. You as commander of the 5th battalion on the basis of this very same radio equipment, did you maintain communications, radio communications, with the command of the 2nd Posavina Brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska whose command was in Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, you were asked by Mr. Pantelic on pages 50 through 54, 55, of the transcript dated the 20th of March, you were asked about reports being submitted to the brigade from the detachment. What were the organs that were in charge of this and so on and so forth. Tell me, do you know that in the brigade, at higher levels, this is done by the security organ and the military police?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That was their part of the job.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that the question of Mr. Pisarevic was not properly translated. He was not referring to reports here on page 37, line 14, he was talking about criminal charges. So this makes sense probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps the counsel can.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that the word "report" was used. Could it kindly be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, please clarify your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did understand that I asked you about criminal reports being filed in the sense of criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, criminal charges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can we agree, then, that the organs or rather the assistant commander for morale for religious and legal affairs in the brigade was not in charge of filing these criminal charges that he had a completely different line of work?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic also asked you, on page 66, lines 4 through 7, of the transcript of the 20th of March, who from the command ordered and whether you ordered Dusanic, Djordje, nicknamed Dzaltara, on the night of the 17th April, to switch off the telephones at the telephone exchange at the PTT in Bosanski Samac, and your answer was that you did not do that. And then you started saying something about something that you knew or rather that you knew Mr. Dusanic. Do you know Mr. Dusanic?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue. Please finish what you were trying to say about Mr. Djordje Dusanic, nicknamed Dzaltara, that Mr. Pantelic asked you about?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to say then that Djordje Dusanic [Realtime transcript read in error "jury gentleman"], nicknamed Dzaltara, would not know how to switch off his very own telephone at home let alone mess around with this at home -- at the telephone exchange. I mean, he worked at the PTT but he worked there as a watchman in the security there. So this man was not capable of doing that and nobody from the 4th Detachment ever gave him any orders of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe, I don't know maybe this needs clarification, on page 38, line 21, the "jury gentleman" nicknamed doesn't make much sense the way it is recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I put the question to you? I asked you about Mr. Djordje Dusanic, nicknamed Dzaltara. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's not a member of any kind of jury?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was some kind of a watchman, a guard, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it is time for a break. Perhaps this would be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we will take our break and continue at 1100.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, on page 27 and 28 of the transcript, you were asked by the Prosecutor about the patrols of the 4th Detachment, about the strength, about the tasks. Now I'd like to ask you a few questions in relation to the patrols. The 4th Detachment of the JNA, until when did it have patrols in the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These patrols, did they only patrol at night?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mostly at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that as of the 17th of April, 1992, there was a reconnaissance squad that was put in operation and what its task was?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the area of defence was taken over by the 4th Detachment, this squad, according to the command -- the order of commander Antic was put into operation and its task was to follow the movements of the forces of the opponent, its amassment, and to report about that to the command of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have one other question to ask you in relation to this. On the 17th of April, 1992, did you know anything about the presence of armed members of Muslims and its unit, and their unit, in the town of Samac where they were, where they were located and so on? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the command of the detachment, we were very worried about the very poor recall of the people who were called to come and join the detachment but during the day we received calls from citizens, from inhabitants, that in the area of park, of the market, there were men, armed men, who were in positions there as they knew each other, these were SDA members, and according to some information, about 100 people were so deployed or positioned in groups around the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last question that I have for you today is the following: In relation to the Prosecutor's question asked on pages 45 through to 48, you explained that liberation, you were even shown a document, that is information P127. You explained what the word "liberation" means in a military sense. Can you tell us, do you know if the term "liberation" was the word that was used generally in all the reports of the Republika Srpska army, in all the official reports, and it was to be used widely in all these reports?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of that. I know that. And any information, any communication, information in the press, on TV, this is the term that entered our language, "the liberation."

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Jovo Savic for giving evidence to the Trial Chamber. We are now finished with your evidence. You may leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, before the next witness is brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Can I just provide you with the proper English translation now of P168? Which at the moment is only an ID document because of the lack of official translation. I gave you a draft translation. The official translation is now available and so the document can fully go into evidence. It's P168. I have sufficient copies here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number confirmed?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be treated as Exhibit P168 and P168 ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On Friday, I informed the Trial Chamber with regard to the status of the rest of the 92 bis statements which should be translated. So this morning I've been informed from the Registry that during the second break, they will be in position to tell me with a higher certainty at what stage are these translations now, so accordingly, I will immediately inform the Trial Chamber. I believe that it could be solved today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well then. Can we have the next witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Lazarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Gavric.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bearing in mind your condition, I'd like to ask you if you can hear me well or you don't understand my question, could you please let me know straight away so that we have no difficulties or unclear things in relation to the transcript. Can you tell me if you can hear me well?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: For the time being, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So that we don't overlap we've already spoken about this, when I finish my question, could you please wait a couple of seconds before answering the question so that there is no overlapping for the record? You will see before you the LiveNote and when the little dot at the end stops, then you can answer.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, can you please give me your full name and last name.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Dusan Gavric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just wait for the question. Can you just go slowly before you give the answer? Thank you. Mr. Gavric, can you tell me when were you born?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: In 1946, on the 13th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me your place of birth.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: The village of Donja Dubica, municipality of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are you living now?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: I am now living in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me about your schooling, where and when you completed your schools.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: I completed higher school for the organisation of labour in the city of Zagreb and that was in the academic year of 1971-72.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now tell me, what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: I'm an engineer of organisation of labour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what is your ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you serve in the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that and when?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: It was in Ribnica near Kocevje in Slovenia, Kocevje in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your service in the Yugoslav People's Army, did you obtain any rank or any post?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you a couple of questions in relation to your political activity. Can you tell me if you were a member of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia and if you were, when and until when?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was a member of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia in the period between 1968 to 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After 1990, were you a member of any other political party?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, you are not a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, before the 19th of April, 1992, can you tell me where did you live?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
