utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I don't recall the date. I think it was in August. I'm not sure, I can't remember. That was a long time ago. I received a message by courier from the commissioner of the cattle farm in Odzak, Milosevic, Mihajlo, that he immediately needed a plumber to carry out some repair, because he was unable to give water to his cattle that was on the farm, because there were hundreds and hundreds of cattle, it was a very large farm, and because he knew that in Odzak I had these plumbers, he asked me send one good plumber who knew his job. So I called -- in fact I went to the water supply network, where they were, and I asked, Who among you is the best plumber? Because I did not know who was the best -- so this Dasa said I am, so he had more experience, What do I have to do? So I said that he would have to go to this cattle farm there was a problem and there repair would have to be carried out because the cattle were unable to get the water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment. Can you tell us because there is no name in the transcript, who was the person who said who was the best?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: This Dasa, this large man with the mustache, I can't remember his name, his nickname was Dasa, he said that he was the best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was just for the purpose of the record. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Well, he said but I have no tools, I need some tools. So that I could carry out these repairs. So I said where are your tools? He said, The tools were in Samac. So in agreement with Mirko Pavic, and together with the policeman Jacimovic, this person took the car, put Dasa in the car, they went to Samac, then to Novi Grad to carry out the repairs, and when they repaired this thing, then Dasa was brought back to Odzak together with Jacimovic who returned as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell us now, let's leave the water supply system aside, what was the other work that you were in charge of as commissioner for the local commune of Odzak? What did Savo Popovic tell you? What else were you supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: As it is well known, there were commissioners in various companies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please speak slower.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: As far as my line of work was concerned, the further tasks I got were the following: To do a health screening of the population in Odzak, because for the most part they were elderly people and women, because people said that there were some health -- some people with health problems there, heart patients, people with asthma, et cetera, so I carried out this screening. And as I said, there were two heart patients, there were two people with asthma and some other illnesses. We made this list and then we went to the military doctor who worked at the hospital in Odzak at the health centre there. He was very nice, and we agreed that we would bring these people in individually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gavric, please, let's not go into too much detail here. Can you just enumerate these tasks that you were involved in as commissioner?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Well, I can. So it was health. Then also the pensions for pensioners who were receiving pensions and before the war broke out. So I took their last pension cheques, et cetera, and then I was in charge of this procedure. I started sending these to where they were supposed to be sent, and then these people actually started getting their pensions again. Then I also worked on opening store for different goods, so that this would start operating as soon as possible. Then also, I worked on opening the green market, although there weren't all that many inhabitants left but I had the green market cleaned up and also I organised a lavatory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the school year? Did you do anything in terms of schooling?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: The commissioner for education carried out preparations for starting the schools again but there were very few children in Odzak, so schools didn't really start working until 1993. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting to this evidence at all, but it is necessary for you to know when these activities were conducted by this witness. I think it's probably early on in the piece after he returned to Odzak, but I know from notes provided to me by Defence counsel that he remained in Odzak until 1995. And it's important for to you know when these activities were being conducted for the return to normalisation of civilian life. In particular if they were within the indictment period but also if they were soon after his return to Odzak. If all of this is occurring in 1995, it's of no use to us so we have to be clear just a time period on this activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gavric, I assume that this will be our last question for today. You have heard my colleague, the Prosecutor, what he is interested in. So let us just place this within a time frame work. When did you do all of these jobs, in which time period?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: You mean all of it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean in terms of time.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the way it was. When the military council appointed me towards the end of July, at the commissioner in the -- I was commissioner for the local commune of Odzak until the end of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that this has fully clarified the entire situation for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now it's 1345.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes we will rise and continue our proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a second. During the break I was advised by Ms. Registrar to address the Chamber. It's fairly briefly, it's Exhibit P22. I noticed during the reviewing this exhibits that B/C/S version has a small stamp with the time of -- and date of the sending of this telegram, and in English version, we don't have that. So Ms. Registrar was kind to give me this advice to address the Chamber and maybe the interpreters in due course can clarify -- can rectify this translation, just for the sake of the accuracy and list of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you haven't got any information, Mr. Pantelic, about your 92 bis --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately not -- from the Registry they informed me that maybe now we shall get something and I will inform accordingly the Court officer with regard to these statements, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Court will rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
